THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The petitioner-accused is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A & 420 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner- accused-husband used to subject the deceased complainant to NC: 2023:KHC:29406 cruelty, both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
The petitioners-accused Nos.1, 2 and 3 are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 306 r/w Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text:
The case of the prosecution is that, the deceased wife unable to bear the harassment meted out by the accused herein, committed suicide by hanging.
5.

The petitioner-accused and the mother of the deceased are present before this Court, and have filed a joint memo along with an affidavit stating that, they have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and in terms of the settlement, the petitioner No.1 (Crl.P.No.1269/2020) has paid a sum of Rs.6,50,000/- to the mother of the deceased who is present before this Court through demand draft dated 5.7.2023 and Rs.50,000/-by way of cash respectively, and the same is acknowledged by the complainant-mother of the deceased, subject to realization of demand draft.
The complainant has further agreed that, she has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings against the petitioners-accused herein.
6. The Joint memo along with the affidavits are placed on record.

7. The allegation against the petitioners-accused is that they subjected the deceased to cruelty, both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from NC: 2023:KHC:29406 her parental home, and the deceased unable to bear the harassment meted out by the petitioners-accused committed suicide.
8.

The charge sheet does not contain any material that, the petitioners-accused either instigated or abated the deceased to commit suicide nor the petitioner-accused-husband had any knowledge that due to his act the deceased wife would commit suicide.

In the absence of the essential elements so as to constitute the commission an offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the accused will be an abuse of process of law.
9. Offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC, though cognizable and non-compoundable,

however, having regard to the fact that the wife of the accused is no more, and the mother of the deceased who is one of the prosecution witness having settled the dispute amicably with the accused, and also having received a sum of Rs.6,50,000/- towards the expenses incurred for performing the marriage, and having no objection for quashing impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners-accused are subjected to trial, since, the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak, in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.
